text:
omar: Heads-up — after the NVIDIA driver bump to 530.41 in eu-west1 A100 pool, our TRT/xFormers stacks started failing in canary. :rotating_light:

omar: Canary pod crash loop: TensorRT plugin load error, looks like ABI symbol mismatch. Repro on a single A100 node.

omar: Error excerpt:
```
2026-07-19 10:02:12.123 ERROR TRT: /opt/tensorrt/lib/libnvinfer_plugin.so: undefined symbol: _ZN10something::PluginV2...
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what(): TensorRT failed to initialize
```

leah: Which node pool exactly? Did infra roll the driver to all A100s or only a subset? :eyes:

omar: Only the eu-west1-a A100 pool (node-pool-a100-eu). Roll started ~2h ago, ~35% done per infra-bot. Staging A10G pools not touched yet.

devon: FYI I hit a different failure in staging with FlashAttention after a local driver test — CUDA illegal memory access on long sequences (seq_len=4096). Could be kernel/ptx incompat with new driver.

devon: FlashAttn trace:
```
CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
#0 0x7f8b1c... in flash_attn_forward_kernel at flash_attn_kernel.cu:341
#1 0x7f8b2d... in run_forward at attention.cu:88
```

sarah: Is TensorRT package also being updated in the nodes? We ship TRT 8.6 compiled against CUDA 11.8 / driver 525 in our images. If driver moved to 530 but TRT binaries were built against 525, symbol mismatches are expected.

sarah: Also check libcudnn/cublas versions. This smells like an ABI mismatch between the system driver and packaged vendor libs.

infra-bot: rollout-status: eu-west1-a A100 pool upgrade started at 1768803000, completed nodes: 12/34 (35%), strategy: rolling-restart-canary.

devon: Can we just pause the rest of the rollout and pin existing nodes? I can try a quick repro with an image that has TRT rebuilt against 530, but that takes time.

omar: Pausing rollout now. @deploy-bot cancel next 2 upgrade batches and pause node pool upgrade. Need to avoid hitting prod customers.

deploy-bot: Command acknowledged — cancelling upcoming batches (batch 3 and 4). Rollout paused at 35%.

leah: Action plan proposal:
- Stop upgrade on remaining nodes (done).
- Provision a small canary node pool with driver 530 + matching TRT build (or rebuild TRT in a canary image) to see if the mismatch is from TRT or from flash/xformers compiled PTX.
- If TRT can't be rebuilt quickly, fallback: create new node pool with driver 525 and migrate traffic for affected services.
- Create infra ticket to matrix test combos: driver (525/530) x TRT (8.6 built/8.6 rebuilt) x FlashAttention versions x xFormers wheels.

omar: I'm leaning towards fall back to 525 node pool for immediate mitigation. Leah — can infra spin new 525 nodes and cordon the 530 ones?

leah: Yep, I can spin a 525-pinned pool and migrate the canary workload. Will coordinate with SRE to move traffic. Also opening a runbook entry for future driver+trt compatibility checks.

devon: For the repro, I can prepare two containers: one with our current TRT package and one with a locally built TRT against 530, then run the same model load/test. That should tell if the problem is binary incompat or CUDA runtime changes affecting PTX.

sarah: Add this to incident tracker: stack traces, affected models, node pool IDs, driver versions, TRT package versions, and timestamps. We'll need to contact vendor if it's an upstream ABI regression.

omar: Thanks. I'll notify product and impacted customers with a short note. For now: pause rollout, fallback plan = new 525 pool + migrate, sprint to matrix-test. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Note — automated health checks flagged elevated OOM and cuda-internal errors on 4 nodes after upgrade. Keep cordoned nodes isolated.

deploy-bot: Confirmed cancellation. Will re-enable batches once infra signals "safe-to-resume".

leah: I'll follow up with timeline for 525 pool and post a summary in #incidents.

omar: tagging @devon @sarah for followups.
